Direct differentiation yields first two sign-change roots 1/h and (-h+sqrt(h²+8))/2, with primitive identities and stated finite-time laws. Third derivative cubic endpoint signs locate two-to-one interior root transition at cosh t=2. For arbitrary j, periodization ≤ real-line derivative L1 norm, strict cancellation at each positive t and equality in the t→0 limit. Cauchy scaling and an exact total-variation primitive give trig sum; gamma asymptotics give j^-1/2 coefficient. Independently integrated j=1,...,6 Cauchy formula against exact sum (differences ≤9e-9); SymPy t²N2 expansion confirms zero t² term and relative -t⁴/135. Finite checks do not establish all-order strictness, whose analytic argument is supplied.
